REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-54616  Recommendation to approve a Disaster Policy Plan for the Long Beach Continuum
  of Care (CoC) Board and Long Beach Homeless Services to expedite the
  deployment of ESG RUSH.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Amick, Boyce, Lock, Martins, McFadzen, Richert, Tan, Shuford, Wee,
  Rockenbach, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Brezenoff, Diles III, Topolewski, Buenaventura

  • Health Department staff Jeffrey Proctor provided an overview of the Disaster

  Policy Plan. The Emergency Solutions Grant – Rapid Unsheltered Survivor
  Housing (ESG-RUSH) program, created by HUD in 2022, was designed to
  assist people experiencing homelessness (PEH) before and after a natural
  disaster. On January 24th, California Senators Schiff and Padilla announced
  $8M in ESG RUSH funds for the State and Los Angeles County region.
  • Member Lock joined the meeting at 3:18 p.m.
  • Member Richert joined the meeting at 3:22 p.m.
  • Member Tan joined the meeting at 3:23 p.m.
  • HUD provided the City with an award letter January 29th, affirming that the
  City is being awarded $1M to support persons impacted by wildfires and
  straight-line winds. The City's ESG-RUSH allocation plan was shared with
  the board. In addition to the HUD guidance the Policy is intended to align
  with and supplement the board approved 2024 LB CoC Funding Priorities
  Guidance.
  • Members of the board and staff discussed concerns about providers, smaller
  agency regulations and amount of time to spend down.
  • Motion passed, and a roll call vote was taken.
  • A member of the public made a statement expressing their willingness to
  familiarize themselves with the operations and processes of the Long Beach
  CoC.

2.  25-54634  Recommendation to approve the Continuum of Care Duplication of Benefit Policy.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Rockenbach, seconded by Voting
  Member Lewis, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the
  following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Lock, Martins, Richert, Tan, Shuford,  Wee,
  Rockenbach, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Brezenoff, Diles III, McFadzen, Topolewski, Buenaventura

  • Health Department staff Jeffrey Proctor provided an overview of the
  Duplication of Benefit Policy. All federal ESG RUSH and CA CDBG-
  CV subrecipients are required to complete a Duplication of Benefits (DOB)
  analysis for assisted activities to demonstrate that no duplication of benefits
  occurred as defined by HUD ESG-CV and the State of California CDBG-CV
  Duplication of Benefits Policies, respectively.
  • Member McFadzen left the meeting at 3:43 p.m.
  • All providers/entities receiving ESG RUSH and/or CDBG-CV assistance are
  responsible for complying with the requirements set forth in these policies

  and procedures, the State of California’s ESG-CV Duplication of Benefits
  Policy and CPD Notice 21-08.
  • The CoC is responsible for evaluating subawards made to providers or local
  units in government to ensure that duplication of benefits does not exist for
  the entity receiving that award. The CoC is also responsible for monitoring to
  ensure that activities carried out by service providers do not result in a
  duplication of benefits for the program participant in instances stabilization
  services.
  • Health Department staff Jeffrey Proctor provided an overeview of the
  Duplication of Benefit Policy. All federal ESG RUSH and CA CDBG-CV
  subrecipients are required to complete a Duplication of Benefits (DOB)
  analysis for assisted activities to demonstrate that no duplication of benefits
  occurred as defined by HUD ESG-CV and the State of California CDBG-CV
  Duplication of Benefits Policies, respectively.
  • All providers/entities receiving ESG RUSH and/or CDBG-CV assistance are
  responsible for complying with the requirements set forth in these policies
  and procedures, the State of California’s ESG-CV Duplication of Benefits
  Policy and CPD Notice 21-08.
  • The CoC is responsible for evaluating subawards made to providers or local
  units in government to ensure that duplication of benefits does not exist for
  the entity receiving that award. The CoC is also responsible for monitoring to
  ensure that activities carried out by service providers do not result in a
  duplication of benefits for the program participant in instances stabilization
  services.
  • Service Providers are responsible for evaluating housing relocation and
  stabilization services financial assistance.
  • Service providers are responsible for assessing each application to
  determine if any ESG RUSH and/or CDBG-CV assistance will or is likely to
  duplicate financial assistance that has already been received or is likely to be
  received by the program participant.
  • Board members inquired about the technical assistance being offered to
  service providers, specifically regarding expectations and any updates. Staff
  responded that training will be provided to service providers.
  • Motion passed, and a roll call vote was taken.
